description: Issue #838 AC2, the headline: a program may not DECLARE a built-in name, and the profile set it runs under has nothing to do with it. The names cover the ways a name reaches the rule: `forward` is a Turtle & Rendering canonical, `fd` is a Heritage short alias resolving to it (blocked BY CONSTRUCTION, through `canonicalOfHeritageAlias`, never a parallel list), `setxy` is a compact alias spelling that shares a table entry with `set_xy`, `hint` is an Educational meta-command, and `challenge` is a Tutor command. `spec/grammar.md:384` ("`define count`, `define forward`, and `define fd` are equally errors"), `:412` ("what a profile decides is whether a name *works*, never whether a program may declare it") and `:418` (built-in names are versioned with the specification, so an implementation "MUST reject a declaration of exactly that version's built-in names"). Core-only is the assertion that matters here: a fixture run under the full DAG would pass even for an implementation that gated these names per profile. `"check": true` -- a checker rule, nothing is executed and no events are produced.
